value.name: New Mexico New Solar Market Development Tax Credit (NSMDTC) — Battery System
value.administrator: New Mexico Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources Department (EMNRD), Energy Conservation and Management
value.description: Statewide New Mexico income tax credit covering a qualifying solar thermal or PV system AND a paired battery system: 10% of equipment, materials, and labor costs, up to $6,000 total per taxpayer (the cap is shared across the solar+battery system, not $6,000 for each separately). Applications are reviewed first-come-first-served against a $30 million annual statewide aggregate cap. In effect for systems installed 2025 through 2031. Transferable for systems installed since Jan 1, 2022.
value.eligibility: Any New Mexico taxpayer (individual, corporation, or agricultural enterprise) who purchases and installs a qualifying solar thermal, PV, or paired battery system on property in New Mexico, including tribal lands; requires EMNRD certification before claiming via NM Taxation and Revenue Department Form TRD-41406.

battery_programs.notes: Verified directly from EMNRD's own Energy Conservation and Management (ECAM) program page — the same statewide fact already documented in nm-bernalillo-albuquerque-pnm.json. This record's rebates field is already populated by the City's separate Solarize Santa Fe program, so the NSMDTC is recorded only here (battery_programs) rather than duplicating it into rebates as well.

value.name: Solar Escarpment Acknowledgement Letter
value.required_when: for properties within Santa Fe's designated Escarpment overlay area (a City-specific geological/hillside development zone)

required_documents.notes: The City's own 'Construction Permit Submittal Checklists' page lists dedicated checklists for 'Photovoltaic Systems (Roof-Mounted)' and 'Photovoltaic Systems (Ground- or Awning-Mounted),' plus a distinct 'Solar Escarpment Acknowledgement Letter' — a genuinely Santa Fe-specific requirement tied to the city's historic escarpment/hillside terrain protections, not present in any other jurisdiction researched this session. The two PV-specific checklist PDFs themselves were not opened and read this session (time-limited); only their existence and the escarpment-letter requirement are recorded, at reduced confidence, from the checklist index page directly.

value.name: Solarize Santa Fe
value.administrator: City of Santa Fe (Office of Sustainability)
value.description: A city-run bulk-purchasing solar campaign offering negotiated contractor discounts and consumer protections to residents, run in two rounds (2021-2022 and 2022-2023) per the City's own Sustainability Dashboard.

rebates.notes: Status recorded as 'unknown' rather than 'active' since the City's own page describes the 2021-2022 and 2022-2023 campaign rounds in the past tense without stating whether a current/ongoing round exists; not inferred as still active. The same page also states residential solar permits in Santa Fe increased over 780% in the 13 years prior, reaching 4.4 permits per 1,000 residents in 2022 — a City-published adoption metric, not a program itself, so not recorded as a rebate/program entry.
